derived_from.responsibility_boundary: SimpleCoin node (miner.py), wallet client (wallet.py), configuration (miner_config.py); the shipped suite in simpleCoin/tests is the behavior contract

rubrics.criterion: After the solver's patch, no decision point in the node's or wallet's production code branches on a committed configuration literal whose shipped value pins one side unreachable, so no remaining code region's executability depends on a retired feature switch being flipped.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central reachability obligation of the task: the prompt asks for code paths permanently impossible under the committed settings to be unwound, and the case's guard rule reports exactly these disabled regions; an equivalent sound repair either removes such branches or restructures the flow without the switch, and this outcome applies to every one of the three guard flavors in the instance.

rubrics.criterion: No statement in the production modules is positioned after an unconditional return, raise, break, or continue in the same block; the mining handover flow in particular contains no post-termination statement.
rubrics.rationale: The instance's mining flow carries the statement-after-return shape, and the prompt names statements sitting after an unconditional return; this criterion is answerable directly from the solver's patch with the repository's structural tooling and is independent of how any guard was unwound.

rubrics.criterion: Every remaining module-level production symbol - functions, classes, methods, import bindings, and configuration constants in the three production modules - is reachable from the real entry points of the two processes (the node's startup and registered HTTP routes, the wallet's client loop) or directly serves those entry points.
rubrics.rationale: The task's desired outcome is that what remains is what actually executes; the case's never-referenced rule measures exactly this relation, so the criterion can be answered from the checker output over the solver's tree and accepts any sound refactoring that leaves live code wired.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely empty the disabled regions while preserving their wiring: no branch keyed to the old feature switches remains in place with a collapsed body, a comment placeholder, or a pass-through guard.
rubrics.rationale: The plausible near-miss for this instance is collapsing a disabled branch's body and believing the code is gone while the decision point and the switch read survive; the prompt explicitly forbids leaving the branches keyed to retired switches in place, and the instance's guard rule still flags such remnants.

rubrics.criterion: Configuration entries in miner_config.py that existed only to wire the retired machinery (feature switches and their companion timeout values) are removed, while the live settings - miner address, node URL, and peer list - keep their names, values, and consumption unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The cascade obligation: the instance places the retired wiring in the configuration file, so a complete cleanup must carry the configuration with it; the prompt states this explicitly and the behavior suite pins the live values, so this outcome is answerable independently of any file layout choice.

rubrics.criterion: Import statements in the production modules exactly serve the remaining code: no import binding survives whose only consumer was removed, and no import still consumed by live code is dropped.
rubrics.rationale: The instance includes an import binding existing solely for an orphaned wallet helper and a node-side import line extended for retired switches; adjusting import lines is inseparable from removing their consumers and is independently gradable from the patch.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup strands no orphaned machinery: no helper, class, member, or constant survives whose only call sites, constructors, or reads were inside the removed regions.
rubrics.rationale: A realistic incomplete repair removes the visible branch but leaves the function it used to call; the instance deliberately places helpers whose sole references sit in unreachable positions, and the never-referenced rule exposes any straggler, making this failure mode concrete for this case rather than generic.

rubrics.criterion: The repair retires the machinery rather than reviving it: no retired protocol, announcement, panel preview, or alternate validation mode is re-enabled, newly wired, or made reachable through modified plumbing.
rubrics.rationale: The tempting wrong direction in a cleanup around feature switches is to turn them on or reconnect the code instead of deleting it; the prompt's ground rule 'do not re-enable anything retired' makes this instance-specific failure mode part of the obligation, and it is answerable by tracing reachability in the patched tree.

rubrics.criterion: The removal is traceless in the touched regions: no tombstone comments describing deleted code, no stub or no-op wrapper functions left in place of removed bodies, and no placeholder markers where the retired machinery used to live.
rubrics.rationale: The prompt explicitly forbids replacing removed bodies with placeholder comments; the instance's realistic-history style makes comment ghosts the natural residue, so their absence is an instance-specific cleanup outcome rather than a generic style rule.

rubrics.criterion: Remaining documentation in the touched regions describes the code that is actually there: no surviving comment, docstring, or configuration note still presents a removed feature as available, wired, or restorable.
rubrics.rationale: The instance's retired features each arrive with maintainer-style comments (configuration caveats, panel restoration notes, protocol history); a sound cleanup updates the story the files tell, and this is gradable from the patch text alone.

rubrics.criterion: No removed feature survives as a stranded but documented knob: the configuration file does not keep a switch, timeout, or comment for machinery whose implementation was deleted, presented as an option for the future.
rubrics.rationale: The complementary near-miss to R5: deleting the code but keeping the flag 'because we might return to it' leaves the misrepresentation the task exists to remove; the prompt requires that nothing that survives describes features no longer present.

rubrics.criterion: The repository's full recorded test command passes on the solver's tree with the same executed test set as before the repair: the 61 collected tests all pass, none are skipped, deleted, weakened, or newly added to compensate.
rubrics.rationale: The suite in simpleCoin/tests is the shipped behavior contract; the prompt and the case both make passing it unchanged the acceptance line, and preserving the executed set blocks compensatory test edits.

rubrics.criterion: Observable node behavior is unchanged: peer chain fetching still composes from the /blocks API only, chain validation still accepts the peer chains it accepted before, longest-chain consensus answers are identical, the /blocks and /txion endpoints keep their request handling and response shapes, and signature verification behaves exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: Unwinding the disabled guard regions touches the consensus and validation flows at their most answer-sensitive points; the suite pins their observable contract, and this criterion keeps the grader checking the flows themselves so an equivalent restructuring cannot drift behavior while still passing superficial inspection.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup introduces no behavioral residue in the wallet's or node's output and control flow: no announcement or chain-preview output appears on the receipt or mining paths, no extra prompt or print accompanies the documented flows beyond what existed before the cleanup, and no removed helper still contributes to any executed flow.
rubrics.rationale: The retired pieces in this instance are output-adjacent (proof announcements, receipt-time chain previews), so the concrete regression risk is ghost output and side effects reappearing on live paths; this failure mode is specific to the instance and observable by running the documented flows.
